interactions.summary: Jiang invites the class to elaborate alternatives to suicide, and students propose fighting back, dying honorably, or reading Dante as criticism of church doctrine.
A student asks whether randomness or bad luck explains Piccarda's fate, and Jiang turns that proposal back into a question about whether Dante's world allows luck at all.

A student offers the standard explanation that broken vows determine placement, and Jiang refuses to let that answer stand because an all-loving, all-forgiving God still seems to be judging an innocent victim.

claims.claim: Students test whether honorable death in resistance or explicit critique of church teaching could resolve the paradox of forced vows, showing that the class understands the problem as both moral and doctrinal.
Jiang treats the possibility of luck or randomness as a live interpretive issue by asking whether Dante's story-world believes in randomness at all.
A student states the conventional doctrinal reading that the lowest sphere houses people who broke vows, no matter how coercion occurred.
Jiang rejects that conventional reading as insufficient because it conflicts with the class's earlier picture of God as all-loving, all-forgiving, and nonjudgmental.
Jiang insists that Piccarda clearly did nothing wrong, so any placement in a lower sphere still demands a deeper account than simple rule-breaking.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang interrupts the drift toward bad luck by asking whether Dante's cosmos even permits randomness.
signature_moments.source_phrase: does the story believe in in randomness and luck
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It reframes the problem from unfortunate circumstance to the structure of reality in Dante's world.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang forces the contradiction by setting 'all forgiving, all loving' directly against visible judgment.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is the packet's sharpest collision between divine mercy and hierarchical punishment.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The student's summary label for the doctrinal category that supposedly explains why Piccarda remains in the lowest sphere.
A proposed explanatory frame Jiang tests and immediately problematizes by asking whether Dante's universe allows chance.

chronology_notes.note: This June 15 packet records the class moving through failed explanations, from resistance and luck to broken-vow doctrine, before Jiang restates the contradiction between divine mercy and Piccarda's judgment.
